title: Telnet: vSPC: Complete dissection of VMOTION-GOAHEAD and VMOTION-PEER messages.
description:
Dissecting the VMware virtual serial port concentrator (vSPC) messages for `VMOTION-GOAHEAD` and `VMOTION-PEER` is made challenging by the fact that the two fields in those messages ("sequence" and "secret") are of no fixed size and have no delimiter.  The only way to correctly interpret their contents is by comparison against earlier packets in the conversation which carry _only_ the sequence number.  For `VMOTION-GOAHEAD`, this is easy, because a preceding message will be the `VMOTION-BEGIN` message which has only the sequence number, so the length of the contents of the `VMOTION-BEGIN` message is sufficient to decode the `VMOTION-GOAHEAD`.

For two-pass analysis, _any_ of the subsequent messages carrying only the sequence number may be used to obtain the length needed to decode the `VMOTION-GOAHEAD` and `VMOTION-PEER` messages.

----

For one-pass analysis, `VMOTION-PEER` presents a more complex situation: There is (by definition) no earlier message in that _Telnet_ conversation which can be used to derive the length of the sequence number.  The only way to obtain the necessary length value is by tracking the actual _vMotion_ conversation as it moves from one Telnet connection (representing the running "source" VM's connection to the serial port concentrator) to the next (the "destination" VM being initialized and attempting to connect to the serial port concentrator).

To achieve this, a new conversation endpoint type, `CE_BLOB` is created.  Just one address is used to identify the vMotion conversation: The concatenation of the sequence and secret.

The final change in the series makes use of `CE_BLOB` to pass the sequence number length from the "source" Telnet connection to the "destination" Telnet connection, making it possible to decode `VMOTION-PEER` in one pass.  A new `CONVERSATION_VSPC_VMOTION` type is used for these conversations.

----

Testing: Use the attached [vspc-success-and-failure.pcapng.gz](/uploads/9824f992aeea66f2c57c366ed626b0c9/vspc-success-and-failure.pcapng.gz), which shows several synthetic vSPC conversations from a single VM which is migrating in a (fake) datacenter.  The command:

```
tshark -d tcp.port==13370,telnet -O telnet -r vspc-success-and-failure.pcapng.gz
```

should suffice.  Note that only the final change in the series allows the `VMOTION_PEER` commands (e.g. as filtered with `-Y telnet.vmware.cmd==44'`) to be correctly dissected unless you also include the `-2` argument when running `tshark`.

commits_data.title: Telnet: vSPC: Track the "vMotion conversation".
commits_data.message:
Telnet: vSPC: Track the "vMotion conversation".

Fully dissect the VMOTION-PEER message, even in a one-pass dissection or when
the VMOTION-PEER-OK message was not captured.  This requires that we correlate
this Telnet conversation with the earlier one carrying the VMOTION-GOAHEAD
message, and extracting the length of the sequence number from there.

commits_data.title: conversation: Add support for a "blob" conversation-element type.
commits_data.message:
conversation: Add support for a "blob" conversation-element type.

The new CE_BLOB is similar to CE_STRING, but can include zeros within its
value, is not NUL-terminated, and -- because it likely isn't printable text --
is displayed as hexadecimal.

commits_data.title: Telnet: vSPC: Dissect "sequence" and "secret" in easy cases.
commits_data.message:
Telnet: vSPC: Dissect "sequence" and "secret" in easy cases.

For a VMOTION-GOAHEAD message, it is likely that we can use an earlier message
in the same conversation to determine the length of the "sequence" field,
allowing us to fully dissect that message.  In a two-pass analysis, even the
length from the VMOTION-PEER-OK message allows for dissection of the preceding
VMOTION-PEER message.

For decoding the VMOTION-PEER message in one pass, it's going to require a bit
more work -- i.e. tracking the "vMotion conversation" across the two Telnet
conversations.
